facts.raw_span: 1-month history of insidious-onset right lower abdominal pain
lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora
afebrile
blood pressure was 110/80 mmHg
firm, non-tender, mobile mass measuring approximately 12 cm × 10 cm in the right lower quadrant
bimanual pelvic examination confirmed a right adnexal mass
carcinoembryonic antigen 1.14 ng/mL
CA-125 21 U/mL
Transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion measuring 16.1 × 7.9 × 8.1 cm in the abdominopelvic region
a provisional diagnosis of a malignant ovarian tumor
double inferior vena cava was identified, with the left cava draining via the left renal vein to the right-sided cava

concepts.why: The patient presents with a large right adnexal mass and a provisional diagnosis of a malignant ovarian tumor, supported by imaging findings and a solid-cystic lesion in the abdominopelvic region.
The patient's imaging findings show a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion, which could be consistent with an ovarian cystadenoma.
The patient's transvaginal ultrasound shows multiple uterine fibroids, which could be contributing to her symptoms.
The patient's lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora could be consistent with a lymphangioma.

aliases: Anomaly of the inferior vena cava
concepts.why: The patient's double inferior vena cava with the left cava draining via the left renal vein to the right-sided cava is a congenital vascular anomaly.

rationales.F01: Right lower abdominal pain is a common symptom of ovarian tumors
rationales.F02: Lifelong non-pitting edema of the left leg extending to the labia majora may be related to lymphatic malformation
rationales.F05: A firm, non-tender, mobile mass in the right lower quadrant is suggestive of an ovarian tumor
rationales.F09: Multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa are consistent with uterine leiomyoma and ovarian tumor
rationales.F10: A well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion in the abdominopelvic region is highly suggestive of an ovarian tumor
rationales.F11: A provisional diagnosis of a malignant ovarian tumor is based on imaging findings
rationales.F12: A double inferior vena cava is a congenital vascular anomaly
